Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

away adverb

going off: go away, run away

also off you go, run away, away with you

classical

Plaut. Cas. 148: St! tacē atque abī.
Cic. Cat. 1.20: abīre in aliquās terrās (Lewis & Short)

abeō, abīre, abiī, abitum

verb, irregular (like eō)

go away, go off

Latin puts “away” into the verb, with ab- (ā-, abs-, au-): abīre, go away; auferre, take away (see remove); aufugere, run away; āvolāre, fly away (see fly away). Abī! is “go away!”, or, kindly, “off you go”.

Other words

  • apage — away with you!, go away!

    interjection · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 2.1.32: apage tē ā mē (Lewis & Short); Ter. Eun. 5.2.65 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; apud Cicerōnem numquam)

    Greek ἄπαγε; also “away with it!”, refusing something (see yucky).

Examples

  • St! tacē atque abī.

    Shh! Quiet, and off you go.Plaut. Cas. 148

  • Tacē atque abī intrō. — Taceō atque abeō.

    Hush and go inside. — Hushing and going.Plaut. Aul. 103

See also away, remove, put away, fly away, slip away, yucky, go.
